title: A Tracked Vehicle and Its Slip: The Thrust a Track Gets From Soil, the Slip It Costs, and What a Little More Slip on One Side Does to a Straight Line

questions.question: Why must a track slip to give thrust?
options: The thrust is the reaction to shearing the soil, and shearing is a slip

questions.question: On the loose sand, half the largest thrust came at a slip of:
questions.explanation: Most of the thrust is got for the first few percent.

questions.question: A pivot needed how much a track?
options: 32.7 N, against 81.8 N for four wheels
questions.explanation: The weight is spread nearer the middle.

questions.question: Slips of 10 and 20 percent on the two tracks turned a straight command by:
questions.explanation: The track that slips more is slower over the ground.

questions.question: Why can a heading not be held by sending equal commands to two tracks?
options: The slips need not be equal: ground varies from side to side

questions.question: Why are the soil values of the lesson marked typical?
options: They are textbook values for a kind of soil, not those of the soil the robot will drive on
